question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=4$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{27}, & 0<x<3, \\ \frac{9-x}{27}, & 3\le x<9, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{9}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{9}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2x}{27}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{9}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{27}(9-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{2{x}^{3}}{27}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{9}\frac{1}{27}(9{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{54}|}_{0}^{3}+{\frac{1}{27}(3{x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})|}_{3}^{9} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}+\frac{81}{4}-\frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{39}{2}-{4}^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
